lines.text: A teammate spots a bug in the middle of a Slack conversation.
Opening a tracker means a form, a project, and ten lost minutes. The thread moves on.
Agent R Q has a better way. In the workspace channel, just type slash t and a title.
The task is created and assigned to the agent, without leaving the channel.
The agent sees it and starts at once. No handoff, no waiting for triage.
As it works, the agent posts updates in the same thread, for everyone who saw the bug.
Anyone can answer by mentioning Agent R Q. Sam wants a test added, so he asks right there.
The agent reads Sam's reply as part of the task, and adds the test.
If it needs permission for something risky, the approval shows up in the thread too.
Then the task closes, with a summary right where the bug first came up.
The conversation and the work live in the same place. Nothing gets lost.
Keep working where you talk. Try slash t in Slack, at Agent R Q dot com.
